title: autoscale-policy-experiments-mar-2026
content:
Purpose:
Capture raw results and operational notes from a set of autoscaling policy experiments run against the GPU fleet (p4d/p3) across us-west1 and eu-west1. Goal: find a policy that maintains p95 text-gen latency < 220ms for small requests (<= 128 tokens) while reducing idle-GPU cost by >= 12% vs baseline reserved pool.

Experiment summary table (high-level):
NAME,REGION,MIN_GPUS,MAX_GPUS,SCALE_TRIGGER,THRESHOLD,COOLDOWN_SEC,RESULT_COST_DELTA,RESULT_P95_LATENCY,OBSERVATIONS
exp-a-west,us-west1,2,20,utilization,70%,180,-8%,240ms,stable but higher tail
exp-b-west,us-west1,1,16,queue_length,12,120,-14%,260ms,lower cost, latency bump under bursts
exp-c-west,us-west1,2,24,combined(util>60%||queue>8),60%/8,300,-13%,210ms,good tradeoff, smooth scale-up
exp-d-eu,eu-west1,1,12,utilization,65%,150,-9%,230ms,oscillation during EU morning spike
exp-e-eu,eu-west1,0,10,per-model-routing + util,60%,240,-18%,250ms,aggressive savings, unstable for heavy seqs

Notes on measurement methodology:
- Workload: synthetic mix (70% text-gen chat, 20% code-completion, 10% embeddings) replayed from last 30 days production traces (sampled).
- Traffic shape: 5m bursts every 30m to emulate peak.
- Metrics: cost measured as estimated GPU-hours * hourly cost; p95 latency measured at the API layer excluding client-side deserialization.
- Warm cache simulated by starting with KV cache pre-populated for 50% of requests (to reflect steady-state chat sessions).
- Each config run for 48 hours to capture diurnal pattern.

Key findings and anomalies:
1) Single-metric util triggers (utilization only):
   - Pros: predictable scaling behavior for sustained load.
   - Cons: misses short bursty traffic (queue spike) leading to p95 spikes; observed slow scale-up when many cold KV caches needed (exp-a-west).

2) Queue-length triggers (requests waiting):
   - Pros: reacts quickly to bursts, reduces tail latency during spike windows (exp-b-west).
   - Cons: risk of over-scaling if transient bot floods or back-to-back synthetic bursts; requires smoothing to avoid churning.

3) Combined rules (utilization OR queue_length):
   - Most balanced in our tests (exp-c-west). Kept p95 under target ~210ms while still reducing cost ~13%.
   - Recommended base policy for hosted API in us-west1, with tuned cooldown and a small buffer (min_gpus 2).

4) Region-specific behavior:
   - eu-west1 saw more oscillation due to tighter capacity and higher variance in request origins (exp-d-eu).
   - Allowing min_gpus=0 (exp-e-eu) saved most cost but caused cold-start penalty on p95 for long-seq requests; unacceptable for enterprise tier.

Tunable parameters we tested with notes:
- min_gpus (0/1/2): min 2 best for US hosted lowest tail-latency risk.
- max_gpus (10/16/20/24): higher max helpful for sudden sustained peaks but increases worst-case cost.
- util threshold (60/65/70): lower thresholds reduce latency but increase cost. 60% with combined rule worked well.
- queue threshold (6/8/12): 8 requests waiting balanced reactivity/stability.
- cooldown (120/180/300s): longer cooldown reduced oscillations; 300s improved stability but slowed down subsequent scaling when after cooldown.
- scale step: increments of 2 gpus reduced over-shoot compared to 4-gpu steps.

Operational runbook snippets (draft):
- For hosted API us-west1 (PLG tier): base policy = combined(util>60% OR queue>8) with min_gpus=2, max_gpus=24, cooldown=300s, step=+2/-1.
- For Dedicated (enterprise): set min_gpus to committed baseline, allow only manual burst above commit for predictable billing.
- For Private/VPC customers: recommend conservative defaults (min>=1) and expose policy knobs to customer.

Risk and follow-ups:
- Observe oscillations when cooldown < 180s and step size > 2. Add hysteresis to prevent thrash.
- Need anomaly detection to ignore short lived bot floods or replayed traffic.
- Validate with customer traffic (not only synthetic) for Private deployments; schedule two-week canary with three pilot customers.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: push combined-rule policy to canary cluster in us-west1, tag as CANARY-AUTO, monitor for 72 hours. (due 2026-03-18)
- Miguel: add smoothing/hysteresis to queue trigger logic and implement step-limiter (due 2026-03-22).
- Ravi: cost model update to include prefetch and KV-cache penalty for cold starts (due 2026-03-19).
- Sofia: create dashboard panels for per-model cold-start latency and scale events (Grafana) (due 2026-03-16).

Comments to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working sheet; numbers are estimates and not final billing-backed figures.
- Please flag any region-specific constraints (quota, spare capacity pools) that would make recommendations risky.
- If approved, we should run a longer-duration (14d) production shadow for one cluster with customer traffic sampling before wide rollout.
